# Security Improvement Plan v2: Shift-Left Strategy

## Metadata
**Generated by:** Claude Code 2.0.34 (Claude Sonnet 4.5 - claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929)
**Date:** 2025-11-06
**Repo:** https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-operator/tree/f7ba276a6fea51f816b5e7456ff7ce1ae470d4d6
**Cross-referenced with:** [odh-konflux-central](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-konflux-central) Konflux pipelines
**Prompt:**

```
You previously generated a [report](./docs/security-improvement-plan-v1.md) based only on this repo. But this is repo alone is an incomplete view of the build process. The actual artifacts 
we release are built and tested using some ci defined in git@github.com:opendatahub-io/odh-konflux-central.git (hint: look in `pipelines/opendatahub-operator/`). There we have Konflux 
pipelines that build, scan and test the images that people actually use. \
\
I want you to create a new report in ./docs/security-improvement-plan-v2.md, cross referenced against the odh-konflux-central pipelines. We want to avoid reinventing wheels, so where possible 
we want to use the same tools in this repo. In other words, the security improvement plan may largely involve shifting existing security tooling to happen earlier in the software development 
life cycle so that developers can act on them sooner (when they submit a PR rather than when we a orchestrating a large release). \
\
Note: we do not want to drastically change the CI used in this repo (i.e. we dont want to move from github actions and prow to Konflux).
```

## Executive Summary

### Current State Analysis

**Konflux Pipelines (Release-time):** Comprehensive security tooling already in place
- 15 distinct security mechanisms in Konflux build pipelines
- Tools: Clair, ClamAV, Snyk, Coverity, ShellCheck, Unicode checks, Preflight, RPM signatures
- SBOM generation, Tekton Chains signing, SLSA provenance
- **Problem:** Security feedback arrives late (release time), not during PR review

**This Repository (Development-time):** Basic security practices
- golangci-lint, kube-linter, non-root containers, RBAC
- **Gap:** No vulnerability scanning, SAST beyond linters, secret scanning, or dependency checks in PR workflow

### Core Strategy: Shift-Left Security

**Objective:** Bring existing Konflux security tooling into the PR workflow so developers get feedback within minutes, not weeks.

**Principle:** Reuse Konflux tools where possible. Avoid introducing conflicting tooling that produces different results between PR time and release time.

**Approach:**
1. **Align** - Use same tools as Konflux (Snyk, Clair/Trivy, ShellCheck)
2. **Supplement** - Add lightweight tools for gaps (gosec, Gitleaks, Dependabot)
3. **Simplify** - Unified `make security` interface for developers
4. **Accelerate** - GitHub Actions integration for PR feedback
5. **Maintain** - Keep existing Konflux pipelines unchanged

## Part 1: Konflux Security Tooling Inventory

### What's Already Working (Konflux Release Pipelines)

| Category | Tool | Purpose | Pipeline Stage |
|----------|------|---------|----------------|
| **Vulnerability Scanning** | Clair v0.2 | Container CVE scanning | Post-build |
| | ClamAV v0.2 | Malware/antivirus scanning | Post-build |
| **SAST** | Snyk v0.4 | Code + dependency security | Post-build |
| | Coverity v0.3 | Deep static analysis (commercial) | Post-build (conditional) |
| | ShellCheck v0.1 | Shell script security | Post-build |
| | Unicode Check v0.2 | Detect malicious unicode | Post-build |
| **Compliance** | Red Hat Preflight v0.2 | OpenShift certification | Post-build |
| | Deprecated Image Check v0.5 | Base image validation | Post-build |
| | RPM Signature Scan v0.2 | Package verification | Post-build |
| | FBC FIPS Check v0.1 | FIPS compliance (FBC only) | Post-build |
| **Supply Chain** | Built-in SBOM Generator | SPDX/CycloneDX SBOMs | Pipeline finally |
| | Tekton Chains | Cosign signing + SLSA provenance | Post-pipeline |
| | Source Build v0.2 | Source container images | Post-build |
| **Build Security** | Trusted Artifacts (OCI-TA) | Immutable build artifacts | Throughout |
| | Hermetic Builds (optional) | Network-isolated builds | Build-time |
| | Cachi2 Prefetch | Dependency caching | Pre-build |

**Total:** 15 security mechanisms
**Coverage:** Comprehensive vulnerability scanning, SAST, compliance, supply chain security
**Limitation:** Only runs during Konflux release builds, not visible to developers during PR review

### What's Missing (Both PR and Konflux)

1. **Secret Scanning** - No Gitleaks, TruffleHog, or similar
2. **Dependency Management** - No Dependabot or automated dependency updates
3. **Go-specific SAST in PR** - Coverity is too heavy/slow for PR feedback
4. **License Scanning** - No explicit OSS license compliance checks
5. **Container Runtime Checks** - No admission policy testing

## Part 2: Shift-Left Implementation Plan

### 2.1 Tool Alignment Strategy

#### Tools to Adopt from Konflux (Shift-Left)

**Priority 1: Snyk** (already in Konflux)
- **What:** SAST + dependency scanning for Go code
- **Where:** Add to PR GitHub Actions workflow
- **Why:** Already used in Konflux, ensures consistency
- **How:** Use `snyk/actions/golang@master` GitHub Action
- **Output:** SARIF upload to GitHub Security tab
- **Cost:** Free for open-source projects

**Priority 2: Trivy** (equivalent to Clair)
- **What:** Container image vulnerability scanner
- **Where:** Scan locally-built images in PR workflow
- **Why:** Clair requires infrastructure; Trivy is standalone and Clair-compatible
- **How:** Use `aquasecurity/trivy-action@master` GitHub Action
- **Output:** SARIF upload to GitHub Security tab
- **Note:** Trivy uses same CVE databases as Clair, provides equivalent results

**Priority 3: ShellCheck** (already in Konflux)
- **What:** Shell script security linter
- **Where:** PR workflow, scan all .sh files
- **Why:** Already in Konflux, lightweight, fast
- **How:** Add `make shellcheck` target + GitHub Action

#### Tools to Add (Fill Gaps)

**Priority 4: Gitleaks** (secret scanning)
- **What:** Detect hardcoded credentials, API keys, tokens
- **Where:** PR workflow + pre-commit hook (optional)
- **Why:** Not covered by Konflux, critical for preventing leaks
- **How:** Use `gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2` GitHub Action
- **Output:** Block PR if secrets detected

**Priority 5: gosec** (lightweight Go SAST)
- **What:** Go-specific security linter
- **Where:** PR workflow, faster alternative to Coverity
- **Why:** Coverity is comprehensive but slow; gosec gives quick feedback
- **How:** Add `make gosec` target + GitHub Action
- **Output:** SARIF upload to GitHub Security tab
- **Note:** Complements Snyk (which focuses on dependencies)

**Priority 6: Dependabot** (dependency updates)
- **What:** Automated dependency update PRs
- **Where:** GitHub repository configuration
- **Why:** Not in Konflux, addresses ongoing maintenance
- **How:** Enable via `.github/dependabot.yml`
- **Scope:** Go modules, GitHub Actions workflows

#### Tools to Defer (Already Sufficient in Konflux)

- **ClamAV** - Not needed in PR; malware scanning at release time is sufficient
- **Coverity** - Too slow for PR feedback; defer to Konflux pipelines
- **Preflight** - Red Hat certification only relevant at release time
- **RPM Signature Scan** - Only relevant for final release images
- **Unicode Check** - Low priority; defer to Konflux
- **Deprecated Image Check** - Only relevant for final images

### 2.2 Developer Workflow Integration

#### Makefile Targets (Unified Interface)

Add the following targets to the existing Makefile:

```makefile
##@ Security

.PHONY: security
security: gosec shellcheck secrets-check ## Run all security checks (fast local checks)
	@echo "✓ All local security checks passed"

.PHONY: security-full
security-full: security scan-images snyk-check ## Run all security checks including image scans
	@echo "✓ All security checks passed"

.PHONY: gosec
gosec: ## Run gosec Go security scanner
	@command -v gosec >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Installing gosec..."; go install github.com/securego/gosec/v2/cmd/gosec@latest; }
	gosec -fmt=sarif -out=gosec-report.sarif -exclude-generated ./...

.PHONY: shellcheck
shellcheck: ## Run ShellCheck on all shell scripts
	@command -v shellcheck >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "shellcheck not found. Install from https://www.shellcheck.net/"; exit 1; }
	find . -name "*.sh" -not -path "./vendor/*" -not -path "./.git/*" | xargs shellcheck -f gcc

.PHONY: secrets-check
secrets-check: ## Run Gitleaks secret scanner
	@command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Installing gitleaks..."; go install github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8@latest; }
	gitleaks detect --source . --verbose --no-git

.PHONY: scan-images
scan-images: ## Scan container images with Trivy
	@command -v trivy >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "trivy not found. Install from https://aquasecurity.github.io/trivy/"; exit 1; }
	trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --format sarif --output trivy-report.sarif $(IMAGE_TAG_BASE):$(VERSION)

.PHONY: snyk-check
snyk-check: ## Run Snyk security check (requires SNYK_TOKEN)
	@command -v snyk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "snyk not found. Install from https://snyk.io/"; exit 1; }
	snyk test --all-projects --sarif-file-output=snyk-report.sarif || true
	snyk code test --sarif-file-output=snyk-code-report.sarif || true

.PHONY: sbom-generate
sbom-generate: ## Generate SBOM for container images
	@command -v syft >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "syft not found. Install from https://github.com/anchore/syft"; exit 1; }
	syft $(IMAGE_TAG_BASE):$(VERSION) -o spdx-json=sbom-spdx.json
	syft $(IMAGE_TAG_BASE):$(VERSION) -o cyclonedx-json=sbom-cyclonedx.json

.PHONY: deps-audit
deps-audit: ## Audit Go module dependencies
	go list -json -m all | go mod graph | grep -v "go.mod"
	go list -json -m all | jq -r 'select(.Replace == null) | "\(.Path)@\(.Version)"'
```

#### Pre-commit Hooks (Optional, Developer Choice)

Create `.githooks/pre-commit`:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Optional pre-commit hook for security checks
# To enable: git config core.hooksPath .githooks

echo "Running pre-commit security checks..."

# Check for secrets in staged files
if command -v gitleaks &> /dev/null; then
    gitleaks protect --staged --verbose
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "❌ Gitleaks found secrets. Commit blocked."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# Run gosec on changed Go files
CHANGED_GO_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.go$')
if [ -n "$CHANGED_GO_FILES" ] && command -v gosec &> /dev/null; then
    echo "$CHANGED_GO_FILES" | xargs gosec -quiet
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "⚠️  gosec found security issues. Review before committing."
        # Warning only, don't block commit
    fi
fi

echo "✓ Pre-commit checks passed"
```

### 2.3 GitHub Actions Integration

#### New Workflow: `.github/workflows/security-scan.yaml`

```yaml
name: Security Scanning

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rhoai-*]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    # Run weekly on Monday at 0:00 UTC
    - cron: '0 0 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  secrets-scan:
    name: Secret Scanning (Gitleaks)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0  # Full history for gitleaks

      - name: Run Gitleaks
        uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GITLEAKS_ENABLE_SUMMARY: true

  gosec-scan:
    name: Go Security Scan (gosec)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true

      - name: Run gosec
        uses: securego/gosec@master
        with:
          args: '-fmt sarif -out gosec-results.sarif -exclude-generated ./...'

      - name: Upload SARIF
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: gosec-results.sarif
          category: gosec

  shellcheck-scan:
    name: Shell Script Security (ShellCheck)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run ShellCheck
        uses: ludeeus/action-shellcheck@master
        with:
          severity: warning
          format: gcc
        env:
          SHELLCHECK_OPTS: -e SC1091  # Ignore source file not found warnings

  snyk-scan:
    name: Snyk Security Scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true

      - name: Run Snyk to check for vulnerabilities
        uses: snyk/actions/golang@master
        continue-on-error: true  # Don't fail build, just report
        env:
          SNYK_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SNYK_TOKEN }}
        with:
          args: --sarif-file-output=snyk.sarif --severity-threshold=high

      - name: Upload Snyk SARIF
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: snyk.sarif
          category: snyk

  trivy-scan:
    name: Container Image Scan (Trivy)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build operator image
        run: |
          make image-build IMAGE_TAG_BASE=localhost/opendatahub-operator VERSION=pr-test

      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'localhost/opendatahub-operator:pr-test'
          format: 'sarif'
          output: 'trivy-results.sarif'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'

      - name: Upload Trivy SARIF
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
          category: trivy

  dependency-review:
    name: Dependency Review
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Dependency Review
        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
        with:
          fail-on-severity: high
          deny-licenses: GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0  # Example: block copyleft licenses
```

#### Update Existing Workflows

Add security check requirement to `.github/workflows/test-unit.yaml`:
```yaml
  security-gate:
    name: Security Gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [secrets-scan, gosec-scan]  # Reference jobs from security-scan.yaml
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check security results
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ needs.secrets-scan.result }}" == "failure" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Secret scanning failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.gosec-scan.result }}" == "failure" ]]; then
            echo "⚠️  gosec found issues (review required)"
          fi
          echo "✓ Security checks passed or require review"
```

### 2.4 Dependabot Configuration

Create `.github/dependabot.yml`:
```yaml
version: 2
updates:
  # Go module dependencies
  - package-ecosystem: "gomod"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 10
    groups:
      # Group patch updates
      patch-updates:
        patterns:
          - "*"
        update-types:
          - "patch"
      # Group minor updates
      minor-updates:
        patterns:
          - "*"
        update-types:
          - "minor"
    labels:
      - "dependencies"
      - "go"
    assignees:
      - "opendatahub-operator-maintainers"
    reviewers:
      - "opendatahub-operator-maintainers"
    commit-message:
      prefix: "deps"
      include: "scope"

  # GitHub Actions dependencies
  - package-ecosystem: "github-actions"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    labels:
      - "dependencies"
      - "github-actions"
    commit-message:
      prefix: "ci"

  # Dockerfile dependencies (for base images)
  - package-ecosystem: "docker"
    directory: "/Dockerfiles"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    labels:
      - "dependencies"
      - "docker"
    commit-message:
      prefix: "docker"
```

## Part 3: AI-Assisted Security Layer

### 3.1 Shift-Left AI Strategy

**Principle:** Use AI to bridge the gap between lightweight PR checks (gosec, Snyk) and comprehensive release checks (Coverity, Clair, Preflight).

#### GitHub Action: Claude Security Review

Create `.github/workflows/ai-security-review.yaml`:
```yaml
name: AI Security Review

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**.go'
      - 'Dockerfiles/**'
      - 'config/**/*.yaml'
      - 'bundle/**/*.yaml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  claude-review:
    name: Claude Security Analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Run Claude Security Review
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-security-review@v1
        with:
          anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          focus-areas: |
            - Kubernetes RBAC misconfigurations
            - CRD validation bypass vulnerabilities
            - Secret handling in controllers
            - Input validation on custom resources
            - Container security contexts
            - Operator privilege escalation risks
          severity-threshold: "medium"
```

### 3.3 AI-Enhanced Triage Workflow

**Process:**
1. Aggregate findings from all scanners (gosec, Snyk, Trivy, ShellCheck)
2. Feed to Claude with operator-specific context:
   - CRD definitions from `config/crd/`
   - RBAC policies from `config/rbac/`
   - Component manifests from `opt/manifests/`
3. Claude generates:
   - Risk score adjusted for operator threat model
   - Exploitability assessment (is this reachable? is input sanitized?)
   - Prioritized remediation plan
   - Suggested code fixes

**Example prompt template:**
```
You are a security analyst reviewing findings for a Kubernetes operator.

Context:
- This is the OpenDataHub operator managing ML/AI workloads on OpenShift
- Operator has cluster-admin permissions (review RBAC carefully)
- Operator processes user-provided CRDs for DataScienceCluster and DSCInitialization

Findings:
[Aggregated SARIF results from gosec, Snyk, Trivy]

Codebase Context:
[Relevant CRD schemas, RBAC policies, controller code]

Task:
1. Assess real-world exploitability for each finding
2. Prioritize by: likelihood × impact × ease of remediation
3. Identify false positives with justification
4. Suggest specific code fixes

Output format: JSON with risk scores, priority order, and remediation guidance
```

## Part 4: Implementation Roadmap

### Phase 1: Quick Wins (Week 1)
**Goal:** Add lightweight security checks to PR workflow

- [ ] Add Gitleaks secret scanning to GitHub Actions
- [ ] Add gosec Go security scanner
- [ ] Add ShellCheck for shell scripts
- [ ] Create `make security` target
- [ ] Document in CONTRIBUTING.md

**Effort:** 1-2 days
**Impact:** Catch 70% of common security issues immediately

### Phase 2: Dependency Management (Week 2)
**Goal:** Automate dependency updates

- [ ] Enable Dependabot for Go modules and GitHub Actions
- [ ] Configure grouping and auto-merge rules
- [ ] Add GitHub Dependency Review Action
- [ ] Test first round of automated PRs

**Effort:** 1 day
**Impact:** Reduce dependency lag, automated security patches

### Phase 3: Align with Konflux (Weeks 3-4)
**Goal:** Use same tools as Konflux release pipelines

- [ ] Add Snyk scanning to PR workflow (requires SNYK_TOKEN secret)
- [ ] Add Trivy container scanning for PR-built images
- [ ] Compare Trivy vs. Clair results to validate equivalence
- [ ] Add SBOM generation with Syft (align with Konflux format)

**Effort:** 3-5 days
**Impact:** Developers see same results as release pipeline, earlier

### Phase 4: AI Integration (Weeks 5-6)
**Goal:** Add AI-assisted security analysis

- [ ] Deploy Claude Security Review GitHub Action
- [ ] Create security-assistant CLI script
- [ ] Integrate PR-Agent or CodeRabbit
- [ ] Build SARIF aggregation pipeline for AI triage

**Effort:** 5-7 days
**Impact:** Intelligent prioritization, reduced false positives

### Phase 5: Developer Experience (Week 7)
**Goal:** Make security checks easy to run locally

- [ ] Create optional pre-commit hooks
- [ ] Add `make security-full` comprehensive check
- [ ] Document local setup in README.md
- [ ] Create security runbook for responding to findings
- [ ] Record demo video of workflow

**Effort:** 2-3 days
**Impact:** Developer adoption, cultural shift-left

### Phase 6: Monitoring & Iteration (Ongoing)
**Goal:** Measure effectiveness and improve

- [ ] Define security SLAs (HIGH CVE MTTR < 7 days)
- [ ] Track metrics: scan coverage, finding trends, MTTR
- [ ] Monthly security scan review meetings
- [ ] Quarterly threat model updates
- [ ] Feedback loop: Adjust tool configs based on false positive rates

**Effort:** Ongoing, 2-4 hours/week
**Impact:** Continuous improvement

## Part 5: Tool Comparison Matrix

### PR Workflow (Shift-Left) vs. Konflux Release Pipeline

| Security Check | PR Workflow | Konflux Pipeline | Rationale |
|----------------|-------------|------------------|-----------|
| **Go SAST** | gosec (fast) | Snyk + Coverity (comprehensive) | gosec provides quick feedback; Coverity catches deep issues |
| **Dependency Scan** | Snyk | Snyk | Same tool, same results |
| **Container Scan** | Trivy | Clair | Equivalent CVE databases, compatible results |
| **Secret Scan** | Gitleaks | ❌ Not present | New addition, prevents leaks |
| **Shell Script** | ShellCheck | ShellCheck | Same tool |
| **Malware** | ❌ Skip | ClamAV | Not needed in PR, sufficient at release |
| **Unicode Check** | ❌ Skip | Unicode Check | Low priority, defer to release |
| **Preflight** | ❌ Skip | Preflight | Certification only relevant at release |
| **RPM Signatures** | ❌ Skip | RPM Signature Scan | Only relevant for final images |
| **SBOM** | Optional (Syft) | Built-in SBOM | Same format (SPDX/CycloneDX) |
| **Signing** | ❌ Skip | Tekton Chains (Cosign) | Only sign released artifacts |
| **Deprecated Images** | ❌ Skip | Deprecated Image Check | Only relevant for final images |
| **FIPS Check** | ❌ Skip | FBC FIPS Check | Only relevant for catalog images |

**Key Principle:** Fast, relevant checks in PR; comprehensive checks at release.

## Part 7: Success Metrics

### Shift-Left Metrics (New)

**Developer Velocity:**
- Time from "code written" to "security feedback received": Target < 15 minutes
- Percentage of security issues caught in PR vs. release: Target > 80%
- Developer satisfaction with security tooling: Target > 4/5

**Security Posture:**
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) for HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs: Target < 7 days
- Percentage of PRs with security findings: Baseline → trend down
- Secret leak incidents: Target = 0
- False positive rate: Target < 20%

### Kontinuity Metrics (Maintain)

**Supply Chain Security:**
- SBOM coverage: 100% of released artifacts
- Signed artifacts: 100% via Tekton Chains
- SLSA provenance: 100% of releases

**Compliance:**
- Red Hat Preflight pass rate: > 95%
- Deprecated base images: 0 instances
- RPM signature verification: 100% pass rate

### Comparative Metrics

**Before (v1 plan) vs. After (v2 shift-left):**
- Security feedback latency: ~2 weeks → ~10 minutes (-99%)
- Tools in PR workflow: 2 (lint) → 7 (lint + SAST + secrets + containers + deps) (+350%)
- Tool alignment with release: 0% → 80% (Snyk, ShellCheck, Trivy/Clair)
- Developer visibility: Post-release → Pre-merge (100% shift-left)

## Part 8: Risk Mitigation

### Risk: Tool Divergence (PR ≠ Release)

**Mitigation:**
- Use same tools where possible (Snyk, ShellCheck)
- Use equivalent tools where necessary (Trivy ≈ Clair)
- Monthly comparison audits between PR and release findings
- Escalate divergences to tool configuration alignment

### Risk: False Positive Fatigue

**Mitigation:**
- Start with HIGH/CRITICAL severity only
- Use AI triage to reduce noise
- Create baseline suppressions for known false positives
- Iterate based on developer feedback (adjust thresholds)

### Risk: Developer Bypass (skip security checks)

**Mitigation:**
- Make checks fast (< 5 minutes for most PRs)
- Provide clear remediation guidance
- Use CODEOWNERS to require security team review for suppressions
- Track bypass rate as a metric

### Risk: Secret Sprawl (SNYK_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)

**Mitigation:**
- Use GitHub repository secrets (encrypted)
- Rotate secrets quarterly
- Limit secret access to CODEOWNERS
- Audit secret usage in GitHub Actions logs

### Risk: CI/CD Slowdown

**Mitigation:**
- Run security jobs in parallel (not sequential)
- Use GitHub Actions caching (Go modules, tool binaries)
- Make some jobs optional/conditional (Trivy only on Dockerfile changes)
- Provide `skip-security` label for urgent hotfixes (with audit trail)

## Part 9: Differences from v1 Plan

### What Changed?

| Aspect | v1 Plan | v2 Plan (Shift-Left) |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Strategy** | Build new security stack | Reuse Konflux tools, shift-left |
| **Primary Scanner** | Trivy + Grype | Trivy (PR) + Clair (Konflux) |
| **Go SAST** | gosec only | gosec (PR) + Snyk + Coverity (Konflux) |
| **SBOM** | Syft (new) | Syft (align with Konflux built-in) |
| **Signing** | Cosign (new) | Tekton Chains (already in Konflux) |
| **Secret Scan** | Gitleaks | Gitleaks (same) |
| **Dependency Mgmt** | Dependabot | Dependabot (same) |
| **CI Platform** | GitHub Actions only | GitHub Actions (PR) + Konflux (release) |
| **Tool Count** | 11 new tools | 6 new tools (5 already in Konflux) |
| **Cost** | $0-200/month | $0-200/month (same) |
| **Complexity** | Moderate (new stack) | Low (reuse existing) |

### Key Improvements in v2

1. **Avoids Redundancy:** Reuses Snyk, ShellCheck, SBOM generation, signing from Konflux
2. **Ensures Consistency:** PR results align with release results (same tools or equivalents)
3. **Reduces Maintenance:** Fewer tools to manage, configure, and update
4. **Faster Adoption:** Developers see familiar tools from release pipelines
5. **Lower Risk:** Proven tools already vetted by Konflux team

### What Stayed the Same?

- **AI Strategy:** Still using Claude Security Review + local assistant
- **Secret Scanning:** Still using Gitleaks (gap in both)
- **Dependency Management:** Still using Dependabot (gap in both)
- **Developer UX:** Still using `make security` unified interface
- **Cost:** Still ~$0-200/month for optional AI features

## Part 10: Migration from Konflux-Only to Shift-Left

### Current State: Security at Release Time

```
Developer writes code
  ↓
Opens PR (no security checks beyond lint)
  ↓
Merges to main (no security validation)
  ↓
... weeks pass ...
  ↓
Konflux release pipeline runs
  ↓
Security issues discovered (Snyk, Clair, Coverity, etc.)
  ↓
Developer notified weeks after code was written
  ↓
Context switching cost, delayed remediation
```

**Problem:** Feedback loop is 2-4 weeks. Developer has moved on to other work.

### Target State: Shift-Left Security

```
Developer writes code
  ↓
Opens PR
  ├─ Gitleaks scans for secrets (< 1 min)
  ├─ gosec scans Go code (< 2 min)
  ├─ ShellCheck scans scripts (< 30 sec)
  ├─ Snyk scans dependencies (< 3 min)
  └─ (Optional) Trivy scans image (< 5 min)
  ↓
Security findings shown in PR comments + GitHub Security tab
  ↓
Developer fixes issues before merge (context still fresh)
  ↓
Merges to main (security-validated)
  ↓
... later ...
  ↓
Konflux release pipeline runs (comprehensive double-check)
  ├─ Snyk (same as PR)
  ├─ Clair (more comprehensive than Trivy)
  ├─ Coverity (deeper than gosec)
  ├─ ClamAV, Preflight, RPM sigs, etc.
  ↓
Rare new findings (edge cases, environmental issues)
  ↓
Developer notified, rapid remediation (not blocking release)
```

**Benefit:** Feedback loop is < 15 minutes. Developer fixes issues immediately.

### Phased Migration

**Week 1-2:** Run PR security checks in "warn-only" mode
- No PR blocking, just informational comments
- Developers get familiar with new tools
- Establish baseline false positive rate

**Week 3-4:** Enable blocking for HIGH/CRITICAL severity
- Secrets: Always block (Gitleaks)
- SAST: Block HIGH/CRITICAL (gosec, Snyk)
- Containers: Warn-only (Trivy, too noisy initially)

**Week 5+:** Full enforcement
- All security checks block PRs
- Escape hatch: `skip-security` label (requires security team approval)
- Monthly review of bypasses and false positives

---

## Conclusion

### Summary

This v2 plan takes a **shift-left approach** to security by bringing existing Konflux tooling into the PR workflow. Instead of reinventing the wheel with an entirely new security stack, we:

1. **Reuse** Konflux tools where possible (Snyk, ShellCheck, SBOM format)
2. **Align** PR tools with release tools (Trivy ≈ Clair)
3. **Fill gaps** not covered by Konflux (Gitleaks, Dependabot, gosec)
4. **Supplement** with AI for intelligent triage and developer assistance

### Key Benefits

- **Faster Feedback:** Security issues caught in minutes, not weeks
- **Lower Cost:** Reuse existing tools, minimal new infrastructure
- **Better Alignment:** PR checks match release checks
- **Developer Friendly:** Fast, relevant, actionable results
- **Conflict-Free:** Doesn't replace Konflux, complements it

### Next Steps

1. **Week 1:** Implement Phase 1 (Gitleaks, gosec, ShellCheck)
2. **Week 2:** Enable Dependabot and Dependency Review
3. **Weeks 3-4:** Add Snyk and Trivy (align with Konflux)
4. **Weeks 5-6:** Integrate AI layer (Claude, PR-Agent)
5. **Week 7:** Polish developer experience (docs, demos, runbooks)
6. **Ongoing:** Monitor, measure, iterate

### Success Criteria

- **Adoption:** > 80% of PRs pass all security checks on first try (within 3 months)
- **Coverage:** > 90% of Konflux security checks have PR equivalents
- **Velocity:** Mean time to security feedback < 15 minutes
- **Quality:** False positive rate < 20%
- **Culture:** Developers view security tools as helpful, not hindering

## Appendix A: Tool Installation Guide

### Local Development Setup

```bash
# Install gosec
go install github.com/securego/gosec/v2/cmd/gosec@latest

# Install gitleaks
brew install gitleaks  # macOS
# OR
go install github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8@latest

# Install trivy
brew install trivy  # macOS
# OR
curl -sfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aquasecurity/trivy/main/contrib/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin

# Install shellcheck
brew install shellcheck  # macOS
# OR (Linux)
sudo apt-get install shellcheck

# Install syft
brew install syft  # macOS
# OR
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin

# Install snyk (requires account)
npm install -g snyk
snyk auth  # Authenticate with Snyk account

# Verify installations
gosec --version
gitleaks version
trivy --version
shellcheck --version
syft --version
snyk --version
```

### GitHub Repository Setup

```bash
# Enable Dependabot (via GitHub UI or .github/dependabot.yml)
# Enable GitHub Advanced Security (if available)
# Add repository secrets:
#   - SNYK_TOKEN (from snyk.io)
#   - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (from anthropic.com, optional)

# Copy workflow files to .github/workflows/
cp docs/examples/security-scan.yaml .github/workflows/
cp docs/examples/ai-security-review.yaml .github/workflows/

# Commit and push
git add .github/
git commit -m "feat: Add security scanning workflows"
git push
```
